cues: Transition elements have a partly filled d subshell, with chromium and copper as exceptions in configuration and zinc not a typical member.
They are hard, dense, paramagnetic metals with many oxidation states, up to plus seven in manganese.
Their ions form complexes through dative bonds, with shapes set by the coordination number.
Crystal field theory splits the d orbitals into t two g and e g. Electrons jumping across that gap absorb visible light, giving colour.
And variable oxidation states and active surfaces make them excellent catalysts.
text: Let us recap. Transition elements have a partly filled d subshell, with chromium and copper as exceptions in configuration and zinc not a typical member. They are hard, dense, paramagnetic metals with many oxidation states, up to plus seven in manganese. Their ions form complexes through dative bonds, with shapes set by the coordination number. Crystal field theory splits the d orbitals into t two g and e g. Electrons jumping across that gap absorb visible light, giving colour. And variable oxidation states and active surfaces make them excellent catalysts.
